narrative.overview: The evidence is the decoration. This page behaves like a well-written test report rather than a personal website: numbered rows, dated entries, monospaced metadata, hairline rules between classifications, and prose held to a reading measure. Nothing sits on the screen that does not help a reader verify something about the candidate. The system runs in two themes bound to the same semantic token names, so a component never chooses a colour, only a role. Controls are instrumental and precise: every button label, chip, tag, and navigation link is monospace, uppercase, and tracked out, which makes the interface read as instrumentation rather than marketing chrome. The one moment of personality is a + marker that rotates 45° into an x when a row opens.
keyCharacteristics: Report typography: display headings are always uppercase; metadata is always monospace.
One accent colour, used sparingly as a signal — hover, selection, focus, disclosure. Never as scenery.
Flat by construction: depth comes from hairline rules and tonal surface steps, not shadows.
Gently curved or fully pill corners only, in a three-step scale (3px / 6px / pill).
44px hit targets on every primary control, documented in the CSS as a WCAG 2.5.5 commitment.
Motion exists only on interaction: 150ms on state, 280ms on disclosure, and a global reduced-motion guard.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Pass Green is the only accent in the system. A new hue is not a second accent; it is either a neutral role or it is a mistake.

rules.name: The Verdict Not Scenery Rule
rules.body: The accent signals an action, a state, or a heading. Any surface area larger than a button is evidence that the accent is being used as decoration.

rules.name: The Role Not The Hex Rule
rules.body: Components consume --bg, --ink, --accent, --rule. A literal hex inside a component breaks the theme contract, because the dark theme re-binds the name, not the value.

rules.name: The Classification Case Rule
rules.body: Display and Headline are uppercase by contract; Body, Lead, and Title are sentence case. A lowercase section title is a different brand.

rules.name: The Metadata Is Monospace Rule
rules.body: Anything that behaves like a label rather than a sentence is set in the monospace stack with positive tracking. Reading text never is.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Any number that must line up down a column carries tabular-nums, so a list of indices or counts reads as a table.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and stay flat in every state. If a design needs depth, add a hairline or a tonal step before reaching for a shadow.

rules.name: The Border For Structure Rule
rules.body: A 1px --rule border means 'boundary between regions'. It never means 'this is elevated'.

dos: Do consume colour through the semantic names in src/styles/tokens.css and nothing else; the dark theme works only because every role is a re-bound name.
Do keep the two faces in their lanes: Josefin Sans for headings, Inter for reading, monospace for labels. Adding a fourth face, or loading a face from a CDN, is out of system.
Do set Display and Headline in uppercase and Title/Body in sentence case.
Do hold prose to the 68ch measure and the form to its 560px measure.
Do give every pressable control a 44px target, except chips, which stay above the 24px floor.
Do mark depth with a 1px hairline or a tonal surface step; a 2px accent spine marks disclosure.
Do reuse the accordion row for any list of evidence — it is the pattern recruiters already read.
Do use the + → 45° rotation as the only disclosure affordance, and tabular-nums on any number that stands in a column.
Do run state transitions at 150ms and reveals at 280ms on --ease-out, naming each property.
Do test any new screen in both themes and at a mobile width below 768px, where the navigation stops being sticky.
donts: Don't turn this into the SaaS look: no glassmorphism, no backdrop blur, no elevated rounded cards, no violet or blue gradients, no 16px corners on everything. This is a confirmed rejection, not a preference.
Don't apply --shadow-raised to ordinary surfaces. The system is flat by construction; an unused token is not an invitation.
Don't use Pass Green as a large fill, a background band, or a theme. Its scarcity is the signal.
Don't hardcode a hex or an rgb() value in a component; it will silently break the dark theme.
Don't introduce a second accent, a gradient text treatment, or an emoji as an icon.
Don't animate an interactive state with keyframes; transitions retarget, keyframes do not.
Don't add motion that ignores prefers-reduced-motion, and don't rely on motion as the only feedback for a state change.
Don't wrap content in a bordered card when a hairline rule and indentation will do.
Don't put decorative brackets, badges, or icons in headings; the eyebrow already carries the classification.
